newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - April 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - April 12.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Times Of India
DEVE GOWDA GOVERNMENT VOTED OUT

The government of Prime Minister Deve Gowda was voted out of office on Friday night. But before the government lost the vote of confidence it had sought from the lower house, Gowda attacked the Congress party and its president, and ruled out any patch-up. He warned the party against trying to split the United Front coalition in the 10 days left for the day (April 21) set aside for passing the Finance Bill. Though he did not recommend dissolution of the house when he met the President immediately after losing the vote, Deve Gowda's speech left little option for anything but an election.
The Economic Times
BOMBAY BOURSE BOUNCES ON BUDGET PASSAGE NEWS

Pivotals recovered smartly after witnessing a sharp decline during the course of trading on the Bombay bourse (BSE) following speculative buying by local operators. Marketmen attributed the recovery to the fresh move by the speaker for passing the Financial Bill of 1997/98. Reflecting the uptrend, the 30 share BSE Sensitive index opened at 3,573.97, declined sharply by 62 points against the day's opening to touch the day's low of 3,512.05. It later surpassed 3,609 by touching a high of 3,644.24 and closed at 3,633.73, a net gain of 35.36 points.
MARKETS WILL CRASH IF HOUSE IS DISSOLVED

The markets may crash if the Lower House is dissolved without clearing the Finance Bill. Operators felt that the most crucial aspect for the capital markets was the clearance of the budget, which, they said, held great promises. It was felt that a call for fresh polls without approval to the budget would lead to a situation where the country would have to continue with a vote-on-account which would neither help the economy nor the markets.
PREMIER AUTOMOBILES SET TO DRIVE AWAY FROM PEUGEOT

Premier Automobiles (PAL) might pull out of PAL Peugeot, its joint venture with French auto major Peugeot. Once PAL was out, of the venture, Pegueot might up its stake to more than 50 percent in the company, gaining control over it. The public holds about 34 percent. Sources said PAL's decision to focus on its proposed new venture with Fiat SPA to manufacture Palio, mid-size car for the Indian market, was one of the reasons that prompted it to consider pullout. Both the partners were working out a plan to make Premier Automobiles' exit comfortable.
GLASS MAJOR SAINT GOBAIN TO INVEST $300 MILLION IN INDIA

The $18 billion Saint-Gobain is committed to investing around $300 million in India. Investments worth $25 milion have already been tied up in a 650 tonnes per day float glass project in Tamil Nadu. Saint-Gobain's strategy for investment would cover new acquisitions, greenfield projects and development of existing businesses. Saint-Gobain's existing business involvement in India was a 51 percent holding in Grindwell Norton, 26 percent in Atul Glass Industries, six percent in Maharashtra Glass, 100 percent in Bicron products and 26 percent in Winter Misra, apart from a 90 percent shareholding in the float glass project.
Financial Express
FRESH WAVE OF UNCERTAINTY TO HIT MARKETS

Bourses will be open on Saturday after the United Front government was voted out of power late on Friday. Nothwithstanding hopes on the budget front, which was partly discounted in Friday's session, stock markets would have to grapple with a renewed bout of political uncertainty. Trading was expected to be volatile, with the index swinging with every move made in Delhi. The Bombay bourse president said the market would react sharply when it opened on Saturday for a special trading session. He said the future trend of the market was totally uncertain.
INDIA URGED TO BOOST FOREIGN INVESTMENT TO FURTHER REFORMS

As a further step to economic reforms, India should concentrate on encouraging direct foreign investment and other long term capital inflow, a consultant of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) said. He said that capital account convertibility should be pursued in an orderly manner and at a pace that suited the circumstances of individual countries. Further progress in capital account liberalisation should be sequenced carefully and tailored to the pace of progress with fiscal consolidation and strengthening of the domestic banking system, he added.
RATIO OF CURRENT INVESTMENTS LIKELY TO GO UP

The Reserve Bank of India was set to raise the quantum of bank investments in current category. Most bankers felt the ratio of current-to-permanent category of investments would be changed to 60:40 from the present level of 50:50 in the monetary policy for the first half of 1996/97, to be announced on April 15.
Business Standard
KEY GDRS WEAKEN

The Indian global depository receipts (GDR) markets turned weak as reports of parliamentary proceedings unfolded. Almost all the key GDR offerings opened weak in London and remained at levels lower than the previous close throughout the day. By 6:20 in the evening, the mega-issues had recorded prices which were two to three percent lower than previous levels. The Skindia GDR index dipped 1.47 percent to touch 67.47 levels by late evening. Foreign trading interest weakened with investors preferring not to take hasty trading decisions while the future trend at the local markets remained unclear.
FLASH STRIKE BY ATCS DISRUPTS ALL FLIGHTS

The entire air traffic in the country was paralysed following a flash strike by the air traffic controllers (ATCs), who were protesting tile suspension of one of their colleagues. Although Airports Authority of India chairman and managing director revoked the suspension late in the evening, the ATC Guild insisted that the authority give a written undertaking that such an action would never be taken against them.
TELECOM DEPARTMENT MAY SCALE DOWN FIXED-TO-CELL TARIFFS

The Department of Telecommunications (DoT) was willing to reduce the fixed-to-cellular call tariffs introduced last month. DoT was open to the idea of reducing the pulse rate for such calls from the current rate. The pulse rate sets the number of seconds for which a unit call would be billed. It might be reduced to 36/72/96/120 seconds per unit call. Such a scaling down of the pulse rate would result in a substantial reduction in call tariffs. If the pulse rate be scaled down to 36/72/96/120 seconds, the maximum tariff for a similar call would be 6.25 rupees.
PARTIES AGREE TO PASS THREE CLAUSES OF FINANCE BILL

Leaders of all political parties decided in principle to pass three crucial clauses of the Finance Bill after discussion. They also agreed to a special session of the lower house of parliament to pass an appropriation bill. The three clauses of the Finance Bill proposed to be passed were the clause regarding the customs tariff act, the clause on central excise tariff act and the clause on the additional duties of excise (Goods of special importance) act. These clauses came into effect on February 28 and were due to expire after 75 days. The leaders agreed on a three-day session from April 21 to pass a vote on account for four months in case the parliament is dissolved.
The Observer
APEX BANK SHOULD ENSURE POLICY IMPLEMENTATION

The non-banking finance companies (NBFCs) demanded that the Reserve Bank of India while announcing its monetary policies, must also ensure that the policies were implemented strictly by the banks. The NBFCs which were piquant over the prevalent high interest rates, also complained that the RBI's stipulation of a four percent spread, over the prime lending rates were not strictly followed by the banks. The RBI, in its busy-season credit policy for last year, had said that the banks must disclose their prime lending rates, and their interest rates must vary within a band four percent over the prime lending rates.
DAEWOO TO PICK UP EQUITY IN KRISHNA FILAMENTS

Daewoo Corporation entered into a shareholder agreement with Krishna Filaments (KFL) to subscribe to 1.75 million equity shares, at a premium, aggregating 350 million rupees. Daewoo would also appoint one of their nominees on the board of KFL. Daewoo planned to supply machineries worth $24.237 million to KFL's expansion programme and also agreed to pick up 100 percent buy-back for KFL's 8-strand ropes. KFL has taken up an expansion project at an estimated cost of 1.84 billion rupees.
BOMBAY PLAGUED BY POLLUTION: WORLD BANK

Bombay's worsening air pollution has had a major economic and social impact on India's commercial capital in terms of loss of productivity and increased health problems, the World Bank has found. In a study, the bank estimated the health impact of air pollution on Bombay residents caused approximately 2,800 cases of pollution-related premature deaths and the health damage costs were in the region of 18 billion rupees a year. Unless urgent pollution abatement measures were implemented, the city would be in for a major environmental crisis with the rapid expansion of industries and a 103 percent increase in vehicles over the past decade, it warned.
Business Line
TELECOM MAJORS MAY FIND WAY OUT OF FUNDING IMPASSE

Financing plans of cellular telecom promoters in state circles and in a few other projects were set to be firmed up with financial institutions (FIs) close to working out a policy on funding these projects on a non-recourse basis. This followed the announcement of new external commercial borrowings policy which provides a lot of leeway for telecom companies to source overseas funds. Consequently, the quantum of rupee resources which both the cellular and basic services operators would have to raise from Indian lenders would be substantially lower than projected earlier. The lenders had earlier taken the stand that cellular telecom projects would be financed only if the sponsors agreed to furnish a corporate guarantee.
